title: Regarding the Future
html:
Greetings Community,

 

As you might have noticed, no developer-diary has been published. Fact is, sadly: we had to stop the development of Brick-Force. The original developer left us the game in a state that makes it impossible for us to extend or update the game. That means we are not able to apply bugfixes or new content.

 

At the same time, we must announce that our last active member, WashburneX, will leave the game. Support and sales will no longer happen. We hope we will find a solution for the sales, but for the time being, there won’t be any new sales.

 

If you have any support-requests, please ask the remaining community-moderators and your co-players. All request we receive that are not payment-related will not be handled.

 

Regarding the elephant in the room: No, we will not shut down the game yet. We will inform you when the time comes.

 

Thank you all for your loyalty and the fun we had. We hope we can continue to have more of it for a long time to come.

Thanks for everything and till then!

Cheers!

WashburneX & Your Brick-Force-Team

With that mission, he gathered up the best architects and engineers his kingdom could offer, as well as experts from other countries far away. title: Rockscape by apple2018

html:
Once upon a time, there lived a small group of Brick people in a nameless valley. It was quite picturesque: A little river flowed through flower meadows, which were regularly flooded during autumn time; there was an abundance of everything, and the weather was always beautiful. But this paradisiac environment came at a high price. Every few decades, heavy earthquakes threatened the land. One after the next, the people left the valley until only very few were left.

When a particularly heavy earthquake had destroyed almost everything around them, the remaining inhabitants saw no other way but to leave their beloved home. They decided to venture alongside the few rocks that were left and to climb a steep hill, whose top was said to harbour a mysterious portal placed there eons ago by the gods. None, who had gone through ever returned, so it was shrouded in legend. But the brick people saw no other way and got ready to take the dangerous path up to the top. In order to honour their audacious mission, they named the remaining pieces of the valley “Rockscape”.

title: Quechua by Badaboom5
subtitle: Temple of Doom
html:
Badaboom was on holiday with his family in Peru. Reluctantly, he went to visit the Incan city of Machu Picchu, which has stood there for 4000 years. He was fascinated, and wanted to stay and explore for hours, in particular the Incan temple, said to be a place of worship and sacrifice. Back in the hotel that night, Badaboom’s head was filled with questions and thoughts about the Incans. He fell into a fitful sleep.

Suddenly he was awake, woken by drums. He was in a paradise: waterfalls, palm trees, beautiful sunny sky. An Incan appeared before him, and motioned him to follow. He took Badaboom to the Incan temple, which was fully rebuilt and full of Incans bowing down to the middle of the room, where an animal sacrifice was taking place. Badaboom was so confused, but also transfixed by the sight.

Out of nowhere, gunfire was heard, followed by screams. Badaboom knew what was happening, he remembered from the tour guide – The conquistadors had arrived. He picked up a spear to join the fight, when whiteness filled his vision. BEEP BEEP BEEP. He was back in his bed, and the sun was coming in through the blinds of his room. The crazy dream was over.

Now you get to decide how the battle would have turned out! Who will win, the native Incans and their bloody traditions, or the invading Spaniards, intent on looting everything in their path?

Not even fish now live in the clear ponds surrounding the swamp.”

The guide cleared his throat and paused again. After some hesitation, he continued: “There is a myth saying that the swamp is now home to a special type of bees, whose stings will completely cloud peoples’ minds. The infected are said to attack everyone around them … Well, if you ask me, this is just a fairy tale. After all, bees are animals, too, and all animals that once lived here were killed or driven out. Anyway, we should head on to our next attraction, which is only about 20,000 Bricks west of here.” Suddenly, one of the tourists screamed “Ouch!” and touched their arm. “I think something stung me just now.”

Have you ever heard about the Hanging Gardens of Babylon? No? Well, then you will now get an impression of what they might have looked like: with Snaylor’s newest masterpiece Semiramis+. Legend has it that Semiramis was once a mighty queen of the ancient world, who reigned in old Babylon. Back then, the economy flourished, as Babylon was one of the world’s commercial and cultural centres. They were fighting day in, day out, until finally, one fraction settled down in the Northern half, and the other in the Southern half of the castle.

title: New Game Mode: FreeFall
subtitle: The most fun you can have online
html:
FreeFall brings a whole new style of game-play to Brick-Force, as players compete against one another to avoid falling through the map. Equipped with a build gun and a “Fever Bar” that fills as you remove and add bricks to give you a burst of speed, your objective is to remove the ground from other players. This frantic new game mode features Power-Up Boxes which spawn around the map, unlocking tools to help you achieve your goal.

There are several surprises to uncover in the Power-Up Boxes:

  • Pick-up bombs that drop on your enemy
  • Smoke grenades to obstruct their vision of map holes
  • Fever refills that will instantly boost your “Fever-Bar”
  • Wings that give you a limited time to fly
  • Mega-brickgun that will remove a 3 x 3 space
  • Power-up that instantly forces your enemy into the vortex under the map
     

Challenge yourself with your parkour skills and enjoy the excitement of that well timed jump or brick removal, preventing your enemy from landing their jump.

In physics, “freefall” is any motion of a body where its weight is the only force acting upon it. In Brick-Force, FreeFall is our latest bricktastic new game mode.

The most fun you can have online? Play it today, and find out for yourself!

title: "GraveKeep" by GraveBear
subtitle: Battle for the crown
html:
Darkness falls upon the Keep as citizens divide their trust. The news that the heir to the throne is returning has sparked a skirmish within the walls of GraveKeep. The steward does not like the idea of giving up the throne so easily, and has sent his subjects to defend the stronghold. Take up arms and begin the battle in GraveKeep.

GraveBear, inspired by The Lord of the Rings, has broken the kingdom in two, divided by the high Keep. There are several towers, hidden passages, and portals to help secure the battlefield. Explore each of the several paths to catch your enemy off guard.

Prepare yourself for the skill challenge: complete 20 matches in any mode on GraveKeep and earn yourself a 7-day Infernum Match Stick for your efforts.

subtitle: Battle of the Books

The Infernum Community Team

title: Season 3 Arrives in Europe
subtitle: Brick-Force Travels Back in Time
html:
"Brick by brick" - that is how Brick-Force has evolved since the release about a year ago and brought it to a considerable size. Over two million players have registered and created more than one million maps and fought more than four million matches.

On the 22nd of October, 8pm (7pm UK), the new Season 3 – Bricksaga – will be released and will bring you a whole new gaming experience. New bricks, new costumes, new weapons.

Become a noble knight, a powerful mage, a mischievous thief and much more with our medieval costumes and use our whole new Bricksaga weapons to rule the battlefield.

The new portals will allow you to appear right behind an enemy or lure them into nasty spike traps.   • Powerful and magical weapons such as crossbows and wands
  • New stylish outfits and many more matching accessories in a medieval style
  • New , functional Bricks as trap doors, spike traps, doors and windows
  • Conversion to Force Points to simplify everything
  • Redesign of the Itemshop
  • Revised Level Progression
  • Improved Map Manager
  • UI Optimization
     

Check out all the various changes in the Patch Notes.

subtitle: Embrace the cold.
html:
Step into the harsh, Nordic winter on this map by Fleshcult. The setting is a military installation in a remote region of Northern Europe, complete with snow, trees, and steel-reinforced bunkers to keep the cold out.

There are a lot of obstructions in this map, making a sniper rifle probably not the best choice. Close combat and an element of stealth will benefit greatly.

subtitle: Control the island.
html:
The year is 1944. The setting is the small island of Utirik. Codename: Operation Nightfall. Opposing forces meet on the island via heavy cruising ships. The former paradise of this island no longer remains as two teams do battle to fight for survival in the midst of war.

Modeled after a Japanese island in the World War II theater of war, Op. Night. has five secret passageways to be discovered. Use these to surprise your enemies.

Storm the beaches and play 50 matches on Op.Night. this week and a Cirrus 85 (7 days) will await you following your efforts.

subtitle: Explore Brick-Space.
html:
Thanatos is a futuristic outpost dedicated to studying various anomalies in Brick-Space. Exploding and toxic barrels are abundant in this map, which are great to use against your enemy for damage or to simply prevent them from reaching certain areas. Thanatos is separated between the harsh, outdoor terrain and the protective space station, with a series of caves designed to infiltrate the station, so that one team does not have a total advantage.

Head to space for 10 matches played on Thanatos and Captain Brickmonth’s Boosters (7-day) are yours.

title: "Fragment" by MelodyC
subtitle: A city in the sky.
html:

title: Brick-Force in 2013
subtitle: A closer look at the year ahead
html:
Thanks to all of our fans and friends for supporting Brick-Force over the past year. It’s been a bricktastic year for us, since the launch of the closed beta back in February we have seen an overwhelming response, with over 1.5 million registered players building and blasting their way through an impressive 500,000 user-created maps. We’ve been consistently impressed by the creativity and ingenuity of our community.

In the past few months we’ve added pivotal new features such as adjustable gravity, launch pads, new outfits, weapons, exploding barrels, and a new game mode.

Our latest trailer summarizes how we feel about the year 2012:

So, what’s next? We are not slowing down, that’s for sure. With game-changing new features and content in our upcoming add-on, the Bricksaga, we plan to "brick it to the limit" in 2013. To begin with, the new 15 second weapon change feature has just gone live on our servers, where you’ll have the possibility to switch your weapons at the start of a match. We also now have a new and much improved “Quick Join” that will match you with better game rooms.

The outfit and weapon design contest winners have now seen their items officially added to the game. Congratulations to Gravebear and Matiazo! We have also been working hard on additional new outfits and two new seasons for launch during 2013. We want to polish some aspects of the UI and recently we have also taken significant action against cheating.

Later this year,we aim to add better community features, such as the possibility to invite your friends to a match, along with new filters, tags and even descriptions for your maps, to help put map building in the spotlight. We’re also still super excited about the prospect of an ingame achievement system and expanding our clan functionality.

Finally, we are well aware of the mobile compatibility that we announced in 2012. Although we’ve felt that it was important to polish some aspects of the existing game first, it is our goal to bring you mobile features for Brick-Force in 2013.

Prepare to be surprised, delighted and amazed. We think we've got a great year ahead :)

- The Infernum Productions Crew

A helicopter hovering above the city offers an even better view of parking lots, bus stops, a café and a movie theater. Of course, any good city needs some skyscrapers die spice up the scenery.

An amazing 25,000 bricks were used up in the creation of this impressive work of art.

However, the map won’t only appeal to you visually but also with regards to the balanced gameplay. In this urban environment, you can take advantage of both: the high reach of a sniper rifle as well as the force of assault rifles and grenades to enter buildings and pick snipers off their high walls.

Grab yourself some friends and win 10 matches in Team Deathmatch to pass the challenge.

The rewards for this week’s challenge are 10 potions that provide 50 health points for your action panel.

title: "MarsAttack" by Ploxi
subtitle: Get ready to fight for Mars
html:
Okay Soldiers! Buckle up and get ready to move. We’re going to wipe those filthy aliens from the face of the planet!

Ploxi’s new map sends us off to a battle between brick soldiers and aliens. You’ll find everything a real invasion needs: two parties, invaders and defenders, fighting over one planet. Good guys and bad guys: who will you join? Will you side with the brick soldiers or do you prefer to fight with the aliens?

This map has everything you would expect from a fight between two opposing parties on a moon base. Find hidden passages, use a crashed spaceship to hide, check out the helicopter for snipers and don’t forget to take a look at the main attraction: a space station. Polish your guns for some intense firefights and dominate this map!

Grab yourself some friends and win 10 matches in Team Deathmatch to pass the challenge.

The rewards for this week’s challenge are 10 potions that provide 50 health points for your action panel. Prizes will be delivered on Monday, 3 December.

title: Bring color to your life
subtitle: Let your enemies see stars
html:
With today’s patch we’ll experience another optical change: Brick-Force’s combat will become more colorful.

We were inspired by paintball markers and toy guns and so we sent out our elite Brick-Troops, equipped with spray cans, to bring some color to your weapons.

The changes in detail:

  • Bullet holes are now colored, depending on the surface they hit. Now you can recognize how often you actually have missed your target more noticeably.
  • The muzzles received some color changes, as well (i.e. Pistols now have a green muzzle while submachine guns have a red one).
  • In addition we have changed the muzzle flash, which used to be the same for each gun, to make them more individual. Rifles now have a Brickstar star effect while pistols’ muzzles feature bubbles.
  • Weapons in Brick-Force will now be more distinguished. On the battlefield you will now be able to identify firearms by their colors.

title: Matrixius by Anixian
subtitle: A large-scale project that is finally finished!
html:
On our forums, Matrixius has become somewhat of a Brick-Force myth. It has been in development since closed beta and the subject of numerous forum threads with only a handful of screenshots to prove its existence. Today, the myth has been dispelled and Matrixius is available to download.

A whopping 50,000 bricks has gone into this massive map which is truly a sight for the eyes. Nearly all types of bricks are used, as well. Because the map is so large, it’d be in your best interest to bring a sniper rifle into battle.

All players who complete 15 matches on Matrixius this week will be rewarded with a 7-day version of the Orion, a brand new weapon from Season 2: Brickstar.

We hope you all enjoy this map as much as we do, and be sure to give Anixian a shout over on our forums.

title: Community Spotlight: November 2012
subtitle: A monthly roundup of the Brick-Force community.

We’re back again for another edition of the Brick-Force Community Spotlight. This past month was quite a doozy. Lots of bugs were squashed and Season 2 was launched! It was a busy month, to say the least.

subtitle: Compete for real cash prizes

title: Letter to the Community
html:
Dear Brick-Force Community,

Recently your Brick-Force experience has been affected by the spread of a cheating software which made it possible to do certain things the game usually doesn’t allow, e.g. killing your own team members.

For some players, cheating may seem like a trivial or fun sport, but we share the belief that every single cheater can spoil the fun for dozens of honest players. title: E3 Blog Day Three: Build & Destroy
subtitle: Building and Blasting combined!
html:
On the final day of E3, 2012, we spent some time enjoying the new Build & Destroy mode before the first journalists arrived.

This new mode is great fun and the potential is definitely there. For those of you who aren't familiar with Build & Destory, the concept is simple. The map is divided in the center for the first 2 minutes 40 seconds and players must use this time to build as much as they can on their side of the map, before the curtain is raised. 

   

We had a lot of fun trying to set up traps and even tried making "moats" or large holes in the ground. We are sure that clans and teams will come up with some very creative strategies, and we can't wait to see it in action with 16 players!

Imagine the creative possibilities of building with your clan under time pressure!

Throughout the day our E3 meeting room was full of press and players who wanted a chance to check out the game and talk to us about its development. We were flattered by the responses of some of our visitors - one guest even told us on the last day "Brick-Force is the most innovative thing I've seen at E3".

We hope that you'll feel the same way when you get your hands on our new playmodes in the near future!

title: E3 Day Two: Defense Mode in the Spotlight
html:
We ventured out into the heat of the Los Angeles summer on Wednesday morning to experience the second day of our E3 adventure.
 
The convention hall was completely packed and the passion for gaming that we witnessed was inspiring.
 
Showcasing our two brand new game modes for the first time; visitors to our booth were able to get hands-on play time with new content and find out about our future development plans. Visitors such as PC Gamer, MMORPG.com, onRPG and Joystick.fr dropped by on our second day in Los Angeles.

\

After witnessing some super shooting skills, we decided to keep track of how many waves of monsters our visitors managed to defeat. So far, the YouTuber’s from Machinima are the record-holders after they managed to get to the 23rd wave!

The feedback for the new Defense mode was good. The power ups and leveling system was popular, and many seemed to like the fact that map builders can choose the spawn points and routes that the monsters take in their maps.
 
Thank you to Alienware for providing the M17x laptops for the show, and thanks to everyone who stopped by to say hi and check out Brick-Force.
 
We will be back on Thursday, hungry for more!

title: Coming Soon to Brick-Force

User Interface

A new graphical user interface for Brick-Force has been designed by our team in Berlin and is almost ready to be implemented. Our aim is to simplify Brick-Force’s menus, helping with accessibility and user-friendliness. Click on the concept screenshots to see what we have in store.

New Bricks

Stacks of new bricks are planned for the future. Look forward to different styles, more destructible objects and later this year even special “themed” bricks, such as Sci-Fi or Wild West.

New Game Mode: Build and Destroy

Wish you could build and blast at the same time? Currently in development, the build and destroy mode will incorporate elements of both sandbox and shooter in one action-packed package.

New Game Mode: Defense Mode

Originally known as the Bomber Bee Mode and then later as Wave Mode, this cooperative experience has evolved during development. Now with an increased focus on co-op, we look forward to bringing you Defense Mode in the near future.

New Costumes

 

More character customization is planned. Expect new costumes and more ways to personalize your character.

 

New Weapons

You’ve tweeted and posted so many cool ideas for new weapons and we’ve also brainstormed some cool concepts too! We’ve been talking about rail guns, RPGs, rocket launchers and even a banana gun! We can’t confirm anything yet, but one thing is for sure: new weapons are in development!?

Achievements System

Achievements are coming to Brick-Force! Are you ready for a fully-fledged achievement system?

Interactive Bricks

Okay, we’re talking more than just doors and ladders. We’re talking exploding bricks, traps and other crazy functions.

New Skyboxes

The sky’s the limit! New themes are on the horizon.

New function: Invite players to a game

Yep! That’s right… ever been in the middle of an intense shooter session and wanted to bring your best pal into the action to lend you a hand? This feature is in development.

Improved Map Management

Already filled all three map slots? Fear not, we’re planning to increase the number that can be acquired along with a few additional features which should make life easier for map builders.

 

New attributes / Item stats

We told you new items are coming, but what about stats? In the future, we’re going to introduce new functionalities and attributes to various items.

title: Improve Your Game: Hitboxes Explained
html:
During the course of the closed beta we’ve seen numerous discussions emerge regarding the existence or the possible size of hitboxes in Brick-Force.

For those of you who may not know, in shooter games a hitbox is the term used to describe the invisible area in which you can make an impact on a player. In Brick-Force, head shots make a much stronger impact.
 
Some of the more serious players have already recognized that the closer you shoot to the center of an opponent’s head, the higher chance you have of landing a head shot.
 
To demonstrate, here’s a visual representation of a hitbox in Brick-Force. As shown, there’s a smaller area within the head that we’ve labeled the brain. Hitting the brain is often challenging, but will always guarantee a headshot.

title: GDC Wrap-up: Brick-Force on display at the City by the Bay
html:
After 12 hours of flight and countless gaming sessions of Brick-Force in the heart of San Fransisco, Infernum Productions have now completed a week long showcase to journalists at the Games Developers Conference, the largest annual gathering of professional video game developers.


Carter Dotson, the marvellous writer from 148Apps and Android Rundown alongside Infernum PR Manager Josephine Gehrke.

During our week long trip, writers and video journalists visited us from numerous websites including the likes of Curse Gaming, IGN, MMORPG.com and DroidGamers. From our suite on the 17th floor of a famous San Fransisco hotel, we proudly demonstrated Brick-Force’s sandbox and shooter modes and explained some of the different features that players can look forward to.


The wonderful Damon Brown, journalist at PocketGamer alongside Infernum Community Manager, Matt.

Amongst the breezy heat of a San Fransisco afternoon, the Curse Gaming crew arrived with a camera and microphone to film some action, while Justin Davis, the executive editor of IGN Wireless came with a sprinkle of questions about the smartphone and tablet functionality of the world’s first cross-platform sandbox shooter.


Josi at the Curse office with Oliver Quinn, producer and video editor.

There were many highlights of our trip, such as sampling delicious Mexican food, visiting the world famous Morton’s Steak House and riding bicycles over the golden gate bridge. But perhaps the most exciting for us was the sheer enthusiasm which many of our visitors showed after getting a chance to play Brick-Force. Time and time again we heard the same words from our guests; that Brick-Force has a unique flavor, a rare combination of action and creativity that makes it fun to play and gives it immense potential.



Matt chats to the founder and chief editor at DroidGamers, Andrew Huff

We thoroughly enjoyed our trip to the Game Developer’s Conference and would like to extend our thanks everyone who made time amongst their hectic schedule to come and meet us.


The bay at Fisherman's Wharf on the northern waterfront.

So long, San Fransisco!

title: Important: Closed Beta Login Information
html:
Over the past 24 hours we have seen unprecedented traffic on the Brick-Force servers and a very sharp rise in registrations. While many of you are bursting to login to the game and start playing, we’d like to ask you all for your patience in this very busy time.

Players who have registered for the closed beta or redeemed a key on our website will need to wait for their accounts to be unlocked before they can access the game. After you have received your registration confirmation e-mail, you will eventually receive another separate e-mail to confirm your account has been unlocked.

We must release accounts steadily in several waves over the course of the beta phase in order for this to be a smooth and successful beta. Please be patient while waiting for your activation mail during this busy time.

Thanks again for your support. Please find a step-by-step guide to registration below. As always, you can find updates about our progress on the website, Twitter and Official Blog.

Registration Steps:

  • Step 1: Create an account with username, e-mail and password (and a beta key, if you have one).
  • Step 2: Receive the account confirmation e-mail and click on the activation link.
  • Step 3:  Receive registration e-mail containing download link for the Brick-Force client.
  • Step 4: Wait for the third and final e-mail, confirming that you’re account has been unlocked.

title: Closed Beta Launch
subtitle: And new Website
html:
Welcome to our new home; the official hub for everything Brick-Force. It’s a historic day for the world’s first cross-platform sandbox shooter. The website has arrived and closed beta will soon be launching.

You will find all the latest updates on this page, along with the official blog, guides, and soon a community forum, too. In the future, we’ll also have a clan rankings page, map rankings and further features and content.

The Brick-Force Community Manager, Matt, who will oversee a large portion of the blog and news updates, wanted to leave a short message: “I’d like to say a big thank you to everybody who has supported us via social media over the past months. Rest assured, you will still find a good dose of exclusive content on our Facebook and Twitter pages, but the launch of website will mean that we’ll be able to provide you with a whole bunch of new features and functionality. We’re looking forward to organizing our first map-building contests and clan events for the community.”

Stay tuned for the announcement of the Closed Beta launch which will occur later today. If you’d like to learn more, please take a look at the beta FAQ.

Oh, and finally, a big thank you to our web team who have worked so hard on bringing the website together. We can’t wait to see you in-game!
